messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the 03/04 runtime deploy I'm seeing ~12-18% p99 increases for the TP model on our nvlink cluster. Not all jobs, but a noticeable chunk. Starting a thread to triage.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert model=redwood-tp-7b span=2026-03-15..2026-03-16 artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1768612345.tar.gz :warning:

sara: I pulled a flamegraph and a couple of nvprof traces. All-reduce time has a big spike; GPU compute tail also increased. Quick link: https://perf/reports/1768612345

ivan: Quick numbers from local microbench (same model/input):
`allreduce_ms: nvlink-cluster=9.2, pcie-cluster=6.8`
That looks backwards — NVLink should be lower. Suspect topology routing making NVLink hosts route across PCIe.

jess: Noted. The new kernel selection heuristic (landed in kernel-heuristic-2026-03-04) chooses an FP16 matmul path that uses reduce-scatter + allgather (NCCL pattern). On clean mesh NVLink that's great, but if NCCL picks a ring that crosses CPU PCIe bridges we can get extra hops. Also saw KV prefetch threads pegging a CPU core and driving host<->GPU link traffic.

sara: Attaching a short profiling snippet from nvprof (trimmed):
```
GPU0: cudaLaunchKernel GEMM_FP16 0.48ms
GPU0: ncclReduceScatter 11.7ms (stall 9.6ms)
GPU0: ncclAllGather 2.3ms
GPU1: ncclRecv 3.1ms wait
GPU1: cudnn_conv_forward 0.37ms
```
Shows large NCCL wait time on GPU0.

alex: Immediate mitigation proposal: 1) force kernel fallback to previous matmul path (env INFER_KERNELS=legacy) for affected pools; 2) disable KV prefetch for TP jobs in canary; 3) run topology-aware vs naive routing canaries. If fallback improves p99 we can roll until root cause identified.

ivan: I'll spin two canaries: nvlink-topo nodes with `topology_aware_routing=on` and another with it off (so NCCL picks default). We'll capture nccl-profiling + nvprof. Scheduling now.

jess: Also add a short microinstrumentation for comm/compute overlap: record CUDA events around NCCL calls and compute kernels and emit overlap_ratio = overlap_time / comm_time. If overlap_ratio < 0.6 mark as bad. Patch ready to apply to the runtime shim.

alex: Good plan. If overlap ratio drops below 0.6 we rollback the kernel heuristic. Who will own the rollback? @sara?

sara: On it. I've pushed a rollback patch: `revert: kernel-heuristic-2026-03-04` and feature flag `KV_PREFETCH_TP=false`. Deploying to canary group now.

perf-bot: canary-report nvlink-canary-1: p99 +3% (topology=on), nvlink-canary-2: p99 -1% (kernels=legacy) logs: s3://redwood-perf/1768612345/canary

alex: Nice — the kernel fallback helping is a strong signal. We'll keep the canary running and prepare a short postmortem. Please include KV cache access traces, NCCL topology graphs (ncclTopoPrint output), and the kernel selection trace. I'll create the doc and tag the infra and runtime owners.

jess: For follow-ups: 1) add topology-aware kernel scoring (penalize cross-socket rings), 2) make KV prefetch backpressure-sensitive (don't prefetch when CPU-GPU link saturated), 3) improve perf dashboards to show comm/compute overlap per route.

ivan: Agreed. I'll upload ncclTopoPrint outputs to the perf bucket and correlate with the bad-run list.

alex: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread for updates — please paste canary diffs here.
